title: Custom Models – Full Control 🧠
description: Subclass tf.keras.Model to encapsulate architectures and define custom train_step.

slides.title: Model Subclassing 🏗️
slides.content:
# Beyond Sequential and Functional

Model subclassing gives the ultimate flexibility:
- Define layers in `__init__`.
- Write the forward pass in `call()`.
- Optionally override `train_step()` and `test_step()` to control training logic while still using `fit()`.

This is how researchers prototype complex ideas.

quizData.question: What advantage does overriding `train_step` in a custom model give?

options.text: You can use the model for inference only
You can customise the training logic while still using model.fit() and callbacks
It eliminates the need for an optimizer

quizData.explanation: Custom `train_step` lets you inject logic (e.g., multiple losses, custom gradient ops) yet retain the convenience of `fit()` and callbacks.

slides.title: Custom train_step Example
slides.content: Override to add gradient clipping and weight decay.
slides.codeSnippet:
class RegularizedModel(tf.keras.Model):
    def train_step(self, data):
        x, y = data
        with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
            y_pred = self(x, training=True)
            loss = self.compiled_loss(y, y_pred, regularization_losses=self.losses)
        trainable_vars = self.trainable_variables
        gradients = tape.gradient(loss, trainable_vars)
        # Gradient clipping
        gradients, _ = tf.clip_by_global_norm(gradients, 1.0)
        self.optimizer.apply_gradients(zip(gradients, trainable_vars))
        self.compiled_metrics.update_state(y, y_pred)
        return {m.name: m.result() for m in self.metrics}

slides.title: When to Subclass Model 📋
slides.content:
# Use when:
- Your architecture has dynamic branching based on input.
- You need a custom `train_step` for research.
- You want to share layers in complex ways.

Otherwise, Sequential or Functional API are simpler and often sufficient.

slides.title: Serialization 🧩
slides.content: Subclassed models are harder to save/load (they rely on Python code). Use `save_weights` and `load_weights`, or export to SavedModel with `@tf.function` decorated methods.
